messages:
pagerduty-bot: INC12345 - High error rate detected in AZ4 egress (network). Alert: elevated 5xx on /api/generate — paging on-call.

oncall-net: ack I'm on it, taking initial triage.

sre-ana: I'm seeing a sharp spike in 5xx + TCP resets from clients with IPv6-preferred routes into AZ4. Graphs show a big jump starting ~first alert time. DNS lookups OK, but TCP sessions failing after path MTU negotiation.

infra-bot: No recent infra deploys in the window. No autoscaler activity flagged.

oncall-net: I grabbed an edge pcap from the AZ4 vrouter. Seeing lots of ICMPv6 "Packet Too Big" (PTB) being generated by downstream devices but not reaching the source. Looks like PTB replies are being dropped by an internal firewall/edge appliance.

eng-runtime-john: That matches customer reports about QUIC/TLS handshakes timing out — QUIC relies on PMTUD and fails if PTB is blocked. Also many clients prefer IPv6, so traffic is using the broken path.

support-ops-maya: Impact: multiple enterprise customers in EU reporting realtime disconnects and increased error rates. Support ticket count increased by 5 for affected customers.

oncall-net: Quick mitigation options:
- apply MSS clamp at edge LB (non-disruptive)
- lower MTU on service subnets in AZ4
- force affected services to prefer IPv4 for AZ4

region-noc: Applying MSS clamp on AZ4 egress vrouters now (clamp to 1380). Command run:
```
# apply TCP MSS clamp to avoid fragmentation issues
sudo iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
Command output: OK, rules inserted.

oncall-net: Also opened firewall change to allow ICMPv6 PTB (type 2) between internal edges and customer prefixes. Request CHG-9876 created.

sre-ana: Monitoring metrics after MSS clamp — 5xx rate dropped from ~18% -> ~2% within 6 minutes. Latency to most affected clients returned to normal. Some long-lived connections still timing out, those are being force-replaced.

pagerduty-bot: Status update: INC12345 - Mitigation applied (MSS clamp), customer impact reduced. Incident updated to Investigating -> Mitigated.

support-ops-maya: Posting customer message now: "We've identified an IPv6 path MTU issue affecting AZ4. We've applied a temporary mitigation which has restored most traffic. Engineering is working on a permanent fix. We'll follow up with postmortem and affected list." :email:

eng-runtime-john: Suggest we also roll a small change to prefer IPv4 from gateway pods in AZ4 as a secondary mitigation (less reliance on cloud firewall behavior). I can canary this.

oncall-net: Rolling env change canary: `kubectl set env deploy/gateway NET_PREFER_IPV4=true -n infra --record` -> canary 10% started.

region-noc: Firewall team applied temporary allow for ICMPv6 PTB, pending partner review. Change ID CHG-9876. Cloud partner engagement started to understand why PTB got dropped in the first place.

sre-ana: Handing to network oncall for follow-up/partner escalation. @oncall-net please take ownership for post-incident.

oncall-net: Taking ownership. Immediate next steps:
1) collect pcaps and tcpdumps -> saved at `/var/log/pcap/az4-pmtud-1764501234.pcap`
2) escalate with cloud partner to patch virtual firewall behavior (drop vs proxy PTB)
3) propose permanent config: enforce MSS clamp on AZ4 vrouters + doc change
4) propose longer-term: add active PMTUD monitoring alert

support-ops-maya: Customer impact summary for postmortem: 5 enterprise customers affected, peak error window ~15 minutes, degraded realtime for up to 45 minutes for some sessions. Mitigation restored service for most; follow-ups scheduled.

region-noc: Attached logs and tcpdump to ticket. Also captured example of filtered PTB in syslog:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:45Z] DROP src=2001:db8:41::/64 dst=2001:db8:9::/64 proto=58 type=2 reason=policy
```
This indicates the virtual firewall dropped ICMPv6 type=2 (Packet Too Big) on policy.

eng-runtime-john: For the postmortem we should list the mitigation runbook steps used and recommend adding automatic fallback to IPv4 for services that see sustained IPv6 PMTUD failures.

sre-miguel: Acknowledged handoff. I'll own the postmortem and coordinate with network and cloud partner. Please upload affected customer list and runbook steps.

support-ops-maya: Done — customer list and the support message are attached to the incident ticket.

oncall-net: Estimated ETA for permanent fix: 48 hours (partner kernel/fw patch or config change). We'll keep monitoring and update.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC12345 status -> Monitoring. No active paging until further regression.

region-noc: Notes left in ticket and change logs. PCAP path: `/var/log/pcap/az4-pmtud-1764501234.pcap`.

sre-ana: Thanks everyone. Closing active mitigation thread; will reopen if we see regression. Handing long-form follow-up to @sre-miguel and network oncall. :white_check_mark:

sre-miguel: Taking it from here. Will draft timeline and action items for retrospective.

oncall-net: Closing handover. If anyone sees repeat symptoms, ping me directly. :rotating_light:
